newsitem.title: USA: Key US Republican seeks more Clinton budget cuts.
newsitem.headline: Key US Republican seeks more Clinton budget cuts.

text.p: Senate Budget Committee Chairman Pete Domenici said Monday the White House must accept $10 billion to $30 billion worth of additional curbs on the growth in Medicare spending.

Domenici said, "This is the make-it-or-break-it week" in budget negotiations and warned he is ready to cut a deal with conservative Democrats if President Clinton does not give Congress more domestic spending cuts.

Domenici, a New Mexico Republican, told a meeting of the Associated General Contractors that the budget talks, aimed at reaching agreement on a plan to balance the budget by 2002, would continue through Friday.
He outlined major areas of dispute as being the size of tax cuts, the depth of domestic spending cuts and the changes in the Medicare health program for the elderly.
The White House and Congress are to discuss Medicaid and defense programs later Monday.
"Defense is nearly resolved," Domenici said. He later told reporters defense discussions center on the spending in the last years of the five-year budget agreement.
Domenici told reporters there were no plans as yet to meet with President Clinton at the White House.

In his speech, Domenici said, "Clearly, there will be a tax cut." He said Republicans have three main tax cut goals -- to provide a tax cut for families, to cut the capital gains tax rate and index it to inflation, and to give some relief from estate taxes to be paid by small business owners.
Speaking of other domestic spending, Domenici said, "We believe we can save substantially more money than the President suggests."
The budget negotiators are to meet today at 2:30 p.m. EDT (1830 GMT) on Capitol Hill.
